```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE,
                      fig.align = "center")

library(ipumsr)
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)
```

## Load your IPUMS extract

Point `read_ipums_micro()` at the DDI codebook (.xml), not the data file.
Both files live in the `data/` folder and share the same base name.
Change the file name below to match your extract number.

```{r load}
ddi <- read_ipums_ddi("data/cps_00001.xml")
cps <- read_ipums_micro(ddi)   # changed file name

# Peek at what you have
ipums_var_info(cps)
head(cps)

```
```{r}
ipums_val_labels(cps$EDUC)
```
```{r}
print(ipums_val_labels(cps$EDUC), n = 36)
```


## Clean and prepare

Filter to working-age adults (25-64) with valid wage income.
IPUMS uses large numeric codes for missing or not-in-universe values,
so we drop INCWAGE values of 99999998 and above.

```{r clean}
cps_clean <- cps %>%
  filter(
    AGE >= 25 & AGE <= 64,
    INCWAGE > 0 & INCWAGE < 99999998
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    educ_group = case_when(
      EDUC < 6   ~ "Less than high school",
      EDUC == 6  ~ "High school diploma",
      EDUC < 10   ~ "Some college or associate degree",
      EDUC == 10 ~ "Bachelor's degree",
      EDUC == 11 ~ "Graduate degree"
    ),
    educ_group = factor(educ_group, levels = c(
      "Less than high school", "High school diploma",
      "Some college or associate degree", "Bachelor's degree",
      "Graduate degree"
    ))
  )
```

#missing values handled
```{r clean data}
cps_clean <- cps %>%
  mutate(educ = as.numeric(EDUC)) %>%
  filter(
    AGE >= 25 & AGE <= 64,
    INCWAGE > 0 & INCWAGE < 99999998,
    educ >= 2 & educ < 999          # drop NIU (0, 1) and missing (999)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    educ_group = case_when(
      educ <= 71               ~ "Less than high school",
      educ %in% c(72, 73)      ~ "High school diploma",
      educ >= 80 & educ <= 100 ~ "Some college or associate degree",
      educ %in% c(110, 111)    ~ "Bachelor's degree",
      educ >= 120              ~ "Graduate degree"
    ),
    educ_group = factor(educ_group, levels = c(
      "Less than high school", "High school diploma",
      "Some college or associate degree", "Bachelor's degree",
      "Graduate degree"
    ))
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(educ_group))

# Sanity check: every group should have a reasonable count, and no NA row
count(cps_clean, educ_group)
```

## Visualize

Average wage and salary income (INCWAGE) by education group.

```{r plot}
cps_clean %>%
  group_by(educ_group) %>%
  summarize(avg_wage = mean(INCWAGE)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = educ_group, y = avg_wage)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#2C6E9B") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = dollar_format()) +
  labs(
    title = "Average wage and salary income by education",
    subtitle = "US adults ages 25-64, Current Population Survey ASEC",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Average annual wage income",
    caption = "Source: IPUMS CPS, University of Minnesota, www.ipums.org"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 45,
      hjust = 1
    )
  )
```
#meaningful categories
```{r clean plot}
cps_clean %>%
  group_by(educ_group) %>%
  summarize(avg_wage = weighted.mean(INCWAGE, ASECWT)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = educ_group, y = avg_wage)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#2C6E9B") +
  geom_text(aes(label = dollar(avg_wage, accuracy = 1)),
            vjust = -0.4, size = 3.8) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = label_wrap(15)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = dollar_format(),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08))) +
  labs(
    title = "Average wage and salary income rises with education",
    subtitle = "Wage earners ages 25-64, 2025 earnings (CPS ASEC 2026)\nWeighted by ASEC person weight (ASECWT)",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Average annual wage income",
    caption = "Source: IPUMS CPS, University of Minnesota, www.ipums.org"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
```

## Your interpretation

<!-- What does the chart show? -->
Ans: Among wage earners ages 25–64, average annual wage income rises at every education level, from about $46,000 for those without a high school diploma to about $135,000 for those with a graduate degree, nearly three times as much. The biggest single jump is between some college ($66,000) and a bachelor’s degree ($99,000), a gain of about $33,000.
<!-- What is one reason this association might differ from the causal -->
<!-- effect of education on earnings? -->
Ans: This gap is not the causal effect of education because of omitted variable bias (ability bias), people who earn more degrees also tend to have higher ability, motivation, or family resources, which raise earnings on their own. Because those traits are not in the data, the chart attributes their effect to education, so it likely overstates what an extra degree would add for any given person; estimating the causal effect would require a method such as an instrumental variable or a natural experiment.

Data note: the starter code used IPUMS USA education codes; I recoded EDUC to the CPS coding scheme, dropped not-in-universe and missing values, and weighted averages with ASECWT.

## Stretch goals (optional)

1. Weight the estimates with the ASEC survey weight:
   `summarize(avg_wage = weighted.mean(INCWAGE, PERWT))`
2. Fill or facet by SEX. (SEX is a labelled variable; try `as_factor(SEX)`.)

```{r by sex}
cps_clean %>%
  mutate(sex = as_factor(SEX)) %>%
  group_by(educ_group, sex) %>%
  summarize(avg_wage = weighted.mean(INCWAGE, ASECWT), .groups = "drop") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = educ_group, y = avg_wage, fill = sex)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = label_wrap(15)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = dollar_format()) +
  labs(
    title = "Average wage income by education and sex",
    subtitle = "Wage earners ages 25-64, 2025 earnings (CPS ASEC 2026), weighted",
    x = NULL, y = "Average annual wage income", fill = NULL,
    caption = "Source: IPUMS CPS, University of Minnesota, www.ipums.org"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

3. Try a different chart: a boxplot of INCWAGE by educ_group,
   or a scatterplot of INCWAGE by AGE with a smooth line.
